name: android-control
description: Let Claude see and operate an Android phone: fast screen reading, screenshots, tap, type (any language/emoji), swipe, apps. Installs its own adb; no admin rights, no Android SDK.
long_description: Drives an Android phone through Google's adb. On first use it downloads Android platform-tools into your user profile (%LOCALAPPDATA%\android-control-mcp on Windows), so nothing needs admin rights or a PATH change. Connect over Wi-Fi with Wireless debugging (Android 11+, no USB drivers) or over USB. Claude reads the screen as a numbered element list or an annotated screenshot, then taps, types, scrolls, presses keys, and launches apps. A tiny on-phone helper (pushed over adb, not an app install) makes screen reads ~15 ms and screenshots ~0.2 s, with automatic fallback to plain adb. Run the android_doctor tool first.

adb_path.title: adb location (optional)
adb_path.description: Leave blank to auto-install. Otherwise the full path to adb.exe or to a platform-tools folder you already have.

platform_tools_url.title: platform-tools download URL (optional)
platform_tools_url.description: Leave blank to use Google's official download. Set only if your network needs a mirror.
